pages.title: Heritage of Laphroaig Whisky | Laphroaig
pages.description: Laphroaig's own story of the distillery, from its founding by the Johnston brothers.
pages.text:
OUR HERITAGE. THE STORY SO FAR
1745 1815 1836-47 1857 1887-1908 1921 1923 1929 1935 1954-67 1994 1994 2004 2006 2007 2008 2015 2022

LET THERE BE WHISKY
When the law on distilling was relaxed, Islay's whisky makers could set up legal distilleries, among them the brothers who founded Laphroaig's distillery on the island's south coast in 1815.

BECOMING LAPHROAIG
D. Johnston & Co. is the business brothers Donald and Alexander Johnston founded to sell Laphroaig. They leased 1000 acres to rear cattle. By the end of 1815 the whisky was more profitable than farming, and Laphroaig was officially born.

A FAMILY AFFAIR
Donald bought out his brother's share for £350, and Alexander emigrated to Australia. Donald lived only until 1847.

WATER WARS
In 1907 Peter Mackie of Mackie and Co tried to block the Kilbride Stream with rocks; the courts made him put it right. A year later he built a copy of the still house.

A REVOLUTIONARY REBUILD
After buying the land, Ian Hunter, the last of the founding Johnston family to own the distillery, rebuilt parts of it to double output.

A NEW BEGINNING WITH BESSIE
Bessie Williamson became distillery owner in 1954 after Ian Hunter's passing. In the 60s she gradually sold the distillery to Seager Evans & Co. They completed their acquisition in 1967.

In 1994 HRH Prince Charles visited and gave his Royal Warrant, and Friends of Laphroaig was set up. Friends turned 10 on 30th March 2004. In 2006 John Campbell became Distillery Manager, for 16 years. In 2015 Laphroaig marked two centuries. In 2022 Barry MacAffer became Distillery Manager.

pages.title: Laphroaig distillery - Wikipedia
pages.description: Encyclopedia entry on Laphroaig distillery on Islay and its owners.
pages.text:
Laphroaig distillery is a single malt Scotch whisky distillery on Islay, Scotland. It is on the south coast near Port Ellen, at the head of a small bay called Loch Laphroaig. Owner: Suntory Global Spirits. Founded: 1815. Capacity: 3,300,000 litres.

History
The Laphroaig distillery was established in 1815 by Donald and Alexander Johnston, likely of the MacIain of Ardnamurchan branch of Clan Donald. The last of the Johnston family to run it was Ian Hunter, a nephew of Sandy Johnston, who died childless in 1954 and left the distillery to one of his managers, Bessie Williamson.

The distillery was sold to Long John International, a Scottish distiller, in the 1960s. In 1973 Long John International and the distillery were acquired by Whitbread. In 1989 Whitbread sold the distillery to become part of Allied Domecq. Fortune Brands acquired the brand in 2005, one of the brands Pernod Ricard divested to win approval for its takeover of Allied Domecq. Laphroaig received the Royal Warrant of the Prince of Wales in person during a visit in 1994.

Fortune Brands split up in 2011, forming its spirits business into Beam Inc. Beam was then purchased by Suntory Holdings in April 2014.

Laphroaig Quarter Cask was introduced in 2004 and is bottled at 48% ABV. The 18-year-old was discontinued in late 2015. The Friends of Laphroaig Club was set up in 1994 and revamped in 2020.

Managers include Iain Henderson 1989–2002, John Campbell 2006–2021, Barry MacAffer 2021–2024 and George Campbell from 2024.

pages.title: Laphroaig | Scotch Whisky
pages.description: Whiskypedia entry on Laphroaig with its history, timeline and owners.
pages.text:
Laphroaig. Distillery & brand. Region: Islay. Status: Working. Seven stills; capacity over 3m litres per annum. Its own floor maltings supply 20% of its needs.

History
In 1815 brothers Alexander and Donald Johnston built a distillery at Laphroaig. Donald, who ran it, died in 1847 after falling into a vat of boiling pot ale. Donald's great-grandson Ian Hunter changed agent from Peter Mackie in 1908, prompting the building of Malt Mill. In 1924 the stills were increased to four. On his death in 1954 Hunter left the distillery to his secretary Bessie Williamson. American distiller Schenley bought into the distillery in the 1960s, buying it outright in 1967. By the time Bessie retired in 1972 there were seven stills. Jim Beam purchased it from Allied Distillers in 2005. Beam's takeover by Suntory in 2014 gave the group two Islay distilleries.

Timeline
1815 Alexander and Donald Johnston build Laphroaig on Islay
1924 Laphroaig's two stills are increased to four
1954 Hunter dies; Bessie Williamson runs the distillery
1967 Seager Evans & Company, owned by Schenley, buys Laphroaig and increases the stills to five
1975 English brewer Whitbread buys Seager Evans
1989 Whitbread's spirits division is sold to Allied Distillers
2005 Laphroaig moves under the ownership of Fortune Brands (Jim Beam)
2014 Owner Beam Global is bought out by Japanese group Suntory

Owners
Beam Suntory (parent) 2014 - present; Beam 2006 - 2014; Allied Domecq 1994 - 2006; Allied Lyons 1989 - 1994; Whitbread & Co 1975 - 1989; Schenley Industries 1962 - 1975; Bessie Williamson 1954 - 1962; The Johnston Family 1815 - 1954

pages.title: LOCH LAPHROAIG, LAPHROAIG DISTILLERY (LB12435)
pages.description: Listed building record for Laphroaig Distillery at Loch Laphroaig, Islay.
pages.text:
LOCH LAPHROAIG, LAPHROAIG DISTILLERY (LB12435)

Summary
Category C
Date Added 20/07/1971
Local Authority Argyll And Bute
Parish Kildalton
NGR NR 38751 45143

Description
Earlier 19th century. Large complex of buildings. Rubble, harled or lime-washed. Gabled.
DISTILLERY: 3 storeys.
OFFICE: 2 storeys. Forestair to Palladian doorway (modern).

Statement of Special Interest
House was demolished in 1969.

References
RCAHMS Vol 5 No.437

About Listed Buildings
Historic Environment Scotland designates listed buildings of special architectural or historic interest. It recommends designations to the Scottish Government under the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) (Scotland) Act 1997. A listing covers the exterior, the interior and fixed structures. The records are not definitive historical accounts or complete descriptions of the buildings, and details beyond the statutory address have no legal weight. Listed building consent is needed for changes that affect a building's character.

Images: There are no images available for this record.

expected.notes: opened 1815: the official heritage page (founded in 1815; by the end of 1815 Laphroaig was officially born), Wikipedia (established in 1815; Founded: 1815) and ScotchWhisky.com (built in 1815; the 1815 timeline entry). acquired 1967: the official page (Seager Evans & Co completed their acquisition in 1967) and ScotchWhisky.com (Schenley bought it outright in 1967; the timeline names Seager Evans & Company, owned by Schenley); newOwnerName may be Seager Evans & Co or Schenley. acquired 2014: Wikipedia (Beam purchased by Suntory Holdings in April 2014) and ScotchWhisky.com (Beam's takeover by Suntory in 2014; Beam Suntory 2014 - present). A date of 2014-04 also passes.

notes: Conflicts: (1) The 1960s sale. The official page and ScotchWhisky.com name Seager Evans & Co (owned by Schenley) and give 1967; Wikipedia says Long John International in the 1960s; the ScotchWhisky.com owners list starts Schenley in 1962, when it bought in. The official 1967 should win. (2) Whitbread: 1973 on Wikipedia, 1975 on ScotchWhisky.com, both reference pages, so neither clearly wins and the event is optional. (3) The move to Fortune Brands or Beam: Wikipedia and the ScotchWhisky.com history and timeline say 2005, but its owners list starts Beam in 2006. (4) Managers: the official page has Barry MacAffer from 2022; Wikipedia has 2021. (5) The official page lists years such as 1745, 1857, 1921, 1923, 1929 and 1935 only in its year strip, with no event beside them; a writer must not attach a story to a bare year. Optional events: Bessie Williamson taking over in 1954 (all three history pages), the stills increased in 1924, 1967 and 1972, and the 1847 death of Donald Johnston. Traps: the 1907 water dispute and Mackie's 1908 copy still house belong to Lagavulin's Malt Mill; the 1994 Royal Warrant, Friends of Laphroaig (1994, 2004, 2020), the 2004 Quarter Cask, the 2015 bicentenary and the discontinued 18-year-old are brand, award or visitor details, not distillery events. Suntory's 2014 purchase of Beam is a change of owner and fits acquired. The listing record gives Category C, added 20/07/1971; a listing site fact is valid. Its 1969 demolition is of a house, not the distillery. Capacity is not given in litres of alcohol, so no capacity site fact. Peated stores the owner Suntory Global Spirits and laphroaig.com as website. Page texts are reviewed paraphrases of the cited pages, not copies. The 1989 sale is optional: Wikipedia names Allied Domecq (formed only in 1994), the ScotchWhisky.com timeline Allied Distillers, and its owners list Allied Lyons, so no new owner's name is clearly supported.
